newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson says Coors deal trims Q1.
newsitem.headline: Molson says Coors deal trims Q1.

text.p: Canada's Molson Cos Ltd and subsidiary Molson Breweries reported lower first quarter earnings on Thursday, due mainly to a multi-million settlement with American beer giant Adolph Coors Co.
The Toronto-based beer and entertainment company said net income fell to C$18.7 million in the three months ended June 30, from C$20.8 million in the same period a year ago.
First quarter revenues slipped to C$393.3 million from C$399.7 million.
Molson Cos' operating profit fell to C$32.7 million from C$40.7 million in the same quarter last year, reflecting lower beer and entertainment earnings.
"The costs associated with the interim agreement with Coors more than accounted for the decline in brewing profits...," Molson said in a statement.
Molson Breweries, Canada's biggest brewer, reported first quarter net income dropped to C$57.1 million from C$59.4 million in the same period a year earlier.
Molson Breweries is owned 40 percent each by Molson Cos Ltd and Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and 20 percent by Philip Morris Co's Miller Brewing unit.

Molson Breweries reached an interim agreement earlier this year to settle a dispute with Coors and continue to brew and distribute Coors products in Canada. The settlement included a C$100 million payment to Coors.
Molson Cos said lower profits from its sports and entertainment group, which includes the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League, also contributed to the weaker first quarter.
Molson Breweries, which brews Molson Canadian and Molson Dry, said its Canadian market share slipped to 46.8 percent in the quarter from 47.4 percent in the same period last year.
The brewer's total volume in Canada of 2.5 million hectolitres remained stable.
"Although overall market share was below the same period last year, much of this was due to a spate of competitive activities in the major Ontario market...," Molson Breweries said.
During the quarter, Molson and its rival, Labatt Brewing Co, were engaged in a price war in Ontario, Canada's most-populous province. Labatt is a unit of Belgian beermaker Interbrew S.A.
"Molson finished the quarter on an upswing in Ontario and expects the previously strong performance to continue in the months ahead," Molson Breweries said.
